In [[mathematics]], '''Spanier&ndash;Whitehead duality''' is a [[duality theory]] in [[homotopy theory]], based on a geometrical idea that a [[topological space]] ''X'' may be considered as dual to its complement in the ''n''-[[sphere]], where ''n'' is large enough. Its origins lie in [[Alexander duality]] theory, in [[homology theory]], concerning complements in [[manifold]]s. The theory is also referred to as '''''S-duality''''', but this can now cause possible confusion with the [[S-duality]] of [[string theory]]. It is named for [[Edwin Spanier]] and [[J. H. C. Whitehead]], who developed it in papers from 1955.

The basic point is that sphere complements determine the homology, but not the [[homotopy type]], in general. What is determined, however, is the [[stable homotopy type]], which was conceived as a first approximation to homotopy type.  Thus Spanier&ndash;Whitehead duality fits into [[stable homotopy theory]].

== Statement ==
Let ''X'' be a compact [[neighborhood retract]] in <math>\R^n</math>. Then <math>X^+</math> and <math>\Sigma^{-n}\Sigma'(\R^n \setminus X)</math> are [[dual object]]s in the category of pointed [[Spectrum (topology)|spectra]] with the smash product as a monoidal structure. Here <math>X^+</math> is the union of <math>X</math> and a point, <math>\Sigma</math> and <math>\Sigma'</math> are reduced and unreduced [[Suspension (topology)|suspension]]s respectively.

Taking homology and cohomology with respect to an [[Eilenberg–MacLane space|Eilenberg–MacLane spectrum]] recovers [[Alexander duality]] formally.
